Смяна на адреса предизвиква срок, който не зависи от датата върху ARC. Регистрацията пред Националната имиграционна агенция (NIA) се прави до 30 дни, считано от деня след преместването; същото важи за промяна на мястото на работа по [чл. 31, ал. 6 от Закона за имиграцията](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawSingle.aspx?pcode=D0080132&flno=31).

Картата може да изглежда валидна и след прекратяване на работата, обучението или семейното основание. Когато причината за пребиваване отпадне, NIA отменя разрешението и анулира ARC, освен ако не одобри продължаване по някое от законовите основания в [чл. 31](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawSingle.aspx?pcode=D0080132&flno=31). Отпечатаната дата сама по себе си не гарантира престой до нея.

Затова се пазят датираните документи: предизвестие за прекратяване, диплома или удостоверение за завършване, семеен акт и нов договор за наем. Те показват кое събитие е настъпило и кога.

## Различни събития, различни начални дати

| Ситуация | Срок и орган |
|---|---|
| Обичайно удължаване на ARC | През трите месеца преди изтичането и преди края на текущото разрешение, до NIA. |
| Нов адрес или място на работа | До 30 дни от деня след промяната, регистрация пред NIA. |
| Промяна на основанието по чл. 23-1 | До 30 дни от датата на събитието, заявление до NIA. |
| Промяна на основанието извън чл. 23-1 | До 15 дни от датата на събитието се кандидатства пред BOCA или негов клон за нова виза за пребиваване, след което следва процедура пред NIA. |

Петнадесетдневният срок по [чл. 7 от правилника за пребиваване](https://law.moj.gov.tw/ENG/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=D0080129) е за подаване на заявление, не за получаване на издадена виза. Тримесечният прозорец по чл. 9 означава по всяко време в тези три месеца, а не точно три месеца преди края. За промяната на основание по [чл. 23-1](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawSingle.aspx?pcode=D0080132&flno=23-1) денят на събитието се включва в началната точка, за разлика от адресната промяна.

Някои програми отварят по-ранен прозорец. Удължаване на ARC на предприемач за продължаваща дейност в Тайван се подава през четирите месеца преди изтичането. Ако дейността е прекратена, но е необходимо продължаване на пребиваването, отделният път е през трите месеца преди края. И двете правила са в [указанието на NIA за предприемачи](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5385/7244/7250/7317/%E5%B1%85%E7%95%99/348924/). [Подновяването на самата Gold Card](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5385/7244/7250/7317/%E5%B1%85%E7%95%99/406403/) също има четиримесечен прозорец.

## Удължаване при продължаващо основание

Обикновеното заявление включва формуляр, паспорт, настоящ ARC, снимка и актуални доказателства за работата, обучението или семейната връзка. При преместване се добавя нов адресен документ. [Указанието 0902 на NIA](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/141970) разпределя доказателствата по категории.

Те трябва да покриват искания период. При работа се проверява трудовото разрешение, при студент — записването за съответния срок. Ранната подготовка оставя време да се поднови изтичащ документ или да се допълни удостоверението за обучение. Подаденото заявление още не е удължаване.

Всяко удължаване за мандарин следва доказаното записване. Максимумът е шест месеца. Общият престой и пребиваване по този път обикновено са ограничени до две години съгласно [студентското указание](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/417829/cp_news). Този таван не се прилага автоматично върху обучението за степен.

Таксата е 1000 тайвански долара за всяка одобрена година, а по-кратък период се начислява като цяла година по [чл. 3 от стандартите за такси](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=D0080135). Категорията определя колко може да одобри NIA. Заплащането за по-дълъг период не създава право на него.

## Преместване, нов работодател и допълнителна работа

Новият наем или друг адресен документ подкрепя регистрацията пред NIA. Промяната в банката, университета или кадровата система не я замества. Същото разграничение важи и за работата: регистрацията на работното място не е разрешение за работа.

[Чл. 53 от Закона за заетостта](https://law.moj.gov.tw/ENG/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=N0090001) разграничава категориите работници. При прехвърляне към нов работодател по общото правило новият работодател кандидатства и представя доказателство за прекратяване на предишната работа. Това доказателство е свързано с прехвърлянето, а не е общо изискване за всеки допълнителен работодател. Преди започване конкретната работа трябва да бъде обхваната от приложимото разрешение или освобождаване.

## Когато работата, обучението или семейното основание приключи

След дипломиране, прекратяване на работа или семейна промяна ново основание може да се поиска по [чл. 23-1](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawSingle.aspx?pcode=D0080132&flno=23-1) само в изброените там случаи. Извън тях се прилага визовият път по чл. 7 от правилника. И двете процедури включват преглед на допустимостта.

Продължаване по [чл. 31](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawSingle.aspx?pcode=D0080132&flno=31) може да се разглежда при конкретни обстоятелства: смърт на семейния спонсор, домашно насилие при законовите условия, грижа или контакти с деца в Тайван, текущ трудов спор или лечение на трудова злополука. Всяко основание има собствени условия. Развод или трудов спор сам по себе си нито дава автоматично право да се остане, нито прави напускането неизбежно във всеки случай.

Подходящите специалисти могат да кандидатстват преди изтичането по [чл. 17 от Закона за специалистите](https://law.moj.gov.tw/ENG/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=A0030295). Одобреното удължаване е шест месеца от деня след изтичане на предишния ARC или Gold Card. Възможно е още едно, до общо една година. Това не удължава автоматично предишното право на работа и не е подновяване на Gold Card.

За завършилите в Тайван редовно обучение [чл. 11 от правилника](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=D0080129) предвижда при кандидатстване преди изтичането одобрение за една година от деня след предишния край. При необходимост може още едно удължаване, до общо две години. Завършването само на езиков курс не се приравнява на тази диплома.

При трудов или семеен спор, засягащ пребиваването, първоначалното писмо до [wei@hoveringlaw.com.tw](mailto:wei@hoveringlaw.com.tw) може да посочи събитието и датите без паспортен номер и оригинали на лични документи. Консултациите се провеждат на английски, китайски, японски или корейски.

## Нов паспорт, повредена или изгубена карта

Промяната на номера, името или други данни при нов паспорт се отразява в NIA, както обяснява [официалният въпросник](https://news.immigration.gov.tw/EasyPack/Detail/DDA469F4-E2D0-4A98-847C-21432DCC040E?lang=EN). Общият 30-дневен срок за адрес не се пренася автоматично върху всяка паспортна промяна; отделни карти и процедури могат да имат собствени срокове. Старият паспорт или копие помагат да се свържат записите.

При загуба или повреда NIA изисква формуляр, снимка, паспорт и според случая повредената карта, декларация за загуба, полицейски доклад или друго доказателство. Полицейски доклад не е задължителен при всяка загуба. [Чл. 7 от стандартите за такси](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=D0080135) определя 500 тайвански долара за подмяна. Новата карта не удължава пребиваването.

Загубата в чужбина засяга и връщането. [Обявлението на NIA](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5385/7229/7232/368785/) предвижда онлайн заявление или заявление чрез представител в Тайван, с различни изисквания за удостоверяване при собствен и чужд профил. За стари карти на мигриращи работници и разрешения за еднократно повторно влизане има отделни указания. Преди пътуване NIA и компетентното [тайванско представителство](https://www.boca.gov.tw/sp-foof-countrylp-01-2.html) трябва да посочат нужния документ. Възможността за подмяна не гарантира качване на самолет или индивидуално допускане.

## Пътуване преди получаване на новата карта

Разрешението за повторно влизане се придобива преди отпътуване по [чл. 34 от Закона за имиграцията](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawSingle.aspx?pcode=D0080132&flno=34). [Чл. 20 от правилника](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=D0080129) го ограничава до валидността на ARC и го анулира при анулиране на картата. Валиден паспорт и APRC са изключението за постоянно пребиваващия от отделно разрешение за повторно влизане.

Разписка за подадено заявление не е разрешение за повторно влизане. Това важи и когато се чака подновена или подменена карта.

За притежател на валиден ARC или APRC [официалният отговор на NIA за паспорта](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5385/12162/12197/414977/) посочва, че паспортът трябва да е валиден на деня на пристигане, а граничната проверка остава задължителна. Този отговор не се използва при изтекла или изгубена карта, нито при наличие само на разписка.

В конкретно цитираната [онлайн процедура за специалисти и техните семейства](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5382/5385/7244/7250/7317/%E5%B1%85%E7%95%99/httpscoaimmigrationgovtwcoa-frontendforeign-white-collar/) напускането на Тайван по време на прегледа прекратява разглеждането. След повторно влизане лице, което отговаря на условията, може да подаде ново заявление. Това не е обща забрана за пътуване на всички притежатели на ARC, нито обещание, че повторното влизане ще бъде разрешено.

Ако срокът вече е изтекъл, NIA се уведомява незабавно. При престой извън разрешения срок под 30 дни и продължаващо първоначално основание [чл. 31, ал. 3](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawSingle.aspx?pcode=D0080132&flno=31) допуска законовия път за ново кандидатстване след налагане на санкция. Той не удължава задна дата предишното разрешение и не отменя наказанието. При изчисляване на периода за постоянно пребиваване остава и законовото приспадане на една година.

Стъпките за първа карта са описани в [първоначалното заявление](/bg/columns/taiwan-arc-first-application), а за ново основание — сравнението за [работа, обучение и семейство](/bg/columns/taiwan-visa-residence-work-study-family). Преди предстоящо пътуване решаващи са датата на връщане, състоянието на пребиваването и документите, които действително ще бъдат представени на границата.

Правните източници са проверени на 24 октомври 2026 г.; преводът е подготвен на 25 октомври 2026 г. Материалът описва общи процедури и категорийни изключения, без да определя отделен случай. За жителите на континентален Китай, Хонконг и Макао и за гражданите на Република Китай без домакинска регистрация важат отделни режими.

sourceEvidence.text: NIA registration is due within 30 days counted from the day after the change. A new employer may also require work authorization, and a change in the basis for residence may require a separate application. Updating the address or workplace record does not complete those procedures.

Can you stay until the expiry date printed on your Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) if the job, course or family relationship supporting it ends sooner? Immigration Act Article 31 requires the National Immigration Agency (NIA) to revoke residence permission and cancel the card when the reason for residence disappears, subject to the statutory grounds on which NIA may approve continued residence.
Within 30 days counted from the day after the change.
Change of residence reason qualifying under Immigration Act Article 23-1
Application to NIA within 30 days from the event date.
Change of residence reason outside Article 23-1
The residence regulations prescribe a new resident-visa application to BOCA within 15 days from the event, followed by the NIA residence application.

Immigration Act Article 31 governs address and workplace registration; Articles 7 and 9 of the residence regulations govern changes of residence reason and extensions. Address changes are counted from the following day, while the regulations count a change of residence reason from the event date.

Standard extension fees are NT$1,000 per year of approved validity; a shorter period is charged as one year under Article 3 of the immigration permit fee standards. The residence category determines the period NIA may approve. Paying for a longer period does not create an entitlement to it.

Already past expiry? Contact NIA immediately. Article 31 allows a limited reapplication after a penalty when the overstay is less than 30 days and the original residence reason continues. That provision leaves the original expiry date unchanged; it is not an ordinary grace period.

A move requires new address evidence and NIA registration within the 30-day period. Updating a bank, university or employer's records does not complete the immigration registration required by Article 31. Keep the dated submission record.

For a new employer or an additional job, Employment Service Act Article 53 sets requirements that differ by worker category. The new work must be covered by the applicable permit or exemption before it begins. An NIA address or workplace update does not itself authorize that employment.

After graduation, termination of employment or a family-status change, an ARC holder may apply for a new residence basis under Immigration Act Article 23-1 only in the situations that provision lists.

Continued residence may also be available under Article 31, including specified circumstances involving a deceased family sponsor, domestic violence, children in Taiwan, labor litigation or an occupational injury. Each ground has its own conditions, so a divorce or employment dispute alone does not establish either a right to remain or an inevitable obligation to leave.

Qualifying professionals can seek the extension in Foreign Professionals Act Article 17. If approved, it runs for six months from the day after the original ARC or Gold Card expires. One further extension is available, up to a total of one year. Apply before expiry. Graduates have a different extension framework under Article 11 of the residence regulations, with eligibility tied to the completed program; the professional timetable does not apply to every student.

NIA's guide lists the damaged card, a loss declaration, a police report or other evidence as appropriate when an ARC is lost or damaged. Article 7 of the fee standards sets the standard replacement fee at NT$500. Replacing the card does not extend residence.

Re-entry requires valid permission under Immigration Act Article 34. Article 20 of the residence regulations ties that permission to the ARC's validity period and cancels it when the ARC is canceled. The permission recorded with the card therefore needs to cover the intended return date, along with the passport and residence status.

targetEvidence.text: Регистрацията пред NIA се прави до 30 дни, считано от деня след промяната. Новият работодател може да изисква и разрешение за работа, а промяната на основанието — отделно заявление. Адресната регистрация не изпълнява тези процедури.

Смяна на адреса предизвиква срок, който не зависи от датата върху ARC. Регистрацията пред Националната имиграционна агенция (NIA) се прави до 30 дни, считано от деня след преместването; същото важи за промяна на мястото на работа по чл. 31, ал. 6 от Закона за имиграцията.

Картата може да изглежда валидна и след прекратяване на работата, обучението или семейното основание. Когато причината за пребиваване отпадне, NIA отменя разрешението и анулира ARC, освен ако не одобри продължаване по някое от законовите основания в чл. 31. Отпечатаната дата сама по себе си не гарантира престой до нея.
До 30 дни от деня след промяната, регистрация пред NIA.
Промяна на основанието по чл. 23-1
До 30 дни от датата на събитието, заявление до NIA.
Промяна на основанието извън чл. 23-1
До 15 дни от датата на събитието се кандидатства пред BOCA или негов клон за нова виза за пребиваване, след което следва процедура пред NIA.

Петнадесетдневният срок по чл. 7 от правилника за пребиваване е за подаване на заявление, не за получаване на издадена виза. Тримесечният прозорец по чл. 9 означава по всяко време в тези три месеца, а не точно три месеца преди края. За промяната на основание по чл. 23-1 денят на събитието се включва в началната точка, за разлика от адресната промяна.

Обикновеното заявление включва формуляр, паспорт, настоящ ARC, снимка и актуални доказателства за работата, обучението или семейната връзка. При преместване се добавя нов адресен документ. Указанието 0902 на NIA разпределя доказателствата по категории.

Таксата е 1000 тайвански долара за всяка одобрена година, а по-кратък период се начислява като цяла година по чл. 3 от стандартите за такси. Категорията определя колко може да одобри NIA. Заплащането за по-дълъг период не създава право на него.

Чл. 53 от Закона за заетостта разграничава категориите работници. При прехвърляне към нов работодател по общото правило новият работодател кандидатства и представя доказателство за прекратяване на предишната работа. Това доказателство е свързано с прехвърлянето, а не е общо изискване за всеки допълнителен работодател. Преди започване конкретната работа трябва да бъде обхваната от приложимото разрешение или освобождаване.

След дипломиране, прекратяване на работа или семейна промяна ново основание може да се поиска по чл. 23-1 само в изброените там случаи. Извън тях се прилага визовият път по чл. 7 от правилника. И двете процедури включват преглед на допустимостта.

Продължаване по чл. 31 може да се разглежда при конкретни обстоятелства: смърт на семейния спонсор, домашно насилие при законовите условия, грижа или контакти с деца в Тайван, текущ трудов спор или лечение на трудова злополука. Всяко основание има собствени условия. Развод или трудов спор сам по себе си нито дава автоматично право да се остане, нито прави напускането неизбежно във всеки случай.

Подходящите специалисти могат да кандидатстват преди изтичането по чл. 17 от Закона за специалистите. Одобреното удължаване е шест месеца от деня след изтичане на предишния ARC или Gold Card. Възможно е още едно, до общо една година. Това не удължава автоматично предишното право на работа и не е подновяване на Gold Card.

За завършилите в Тайван редовно обучение чл. 11 от правилника предвижда при кандидатстване преди изтичането одобрение за една година от деня след предишния край. При необходимост може още едно удължаване, до общо две години. Завършването само на езиков курс не се приравнява на тази диплома.

Промяната на номера, името или други данни при нов паспорт се отразява в NIA, както обяснява официалният въпросник. Общият 30-дневен срок за адрес не се пренася автоматично върху всяка паспортна промяна; отделни карти и процедури могат да имат собствени срокове. Старият паспорт или копие помагат да се свържат записите.

При загуба или повреда NIA изисква формуляр, снимка, паспорт и според случая повредената карта, декларация за загуба, полицейски доклад или друго доказателство. Полицейски доклад не е задължителен при всяка загуба. Чл. 7 от стандартите за такси определя 500 тайвански долара за подмяна. Новата карта не удължава пребиваването.

Разрешението за повторно влизане се придобива преди отпътуване по чл. 34 от Закона за имиграцията. Чл. 20 от правилника го ограничава до валидността на ARC и го анулира при анулиране на картата. Валиден паспорт и APRC са изключението за постоянно пребиваващия от отделно разрешение за повторно влизане.

Ако срокът вече е изтекъл, NIA се уведомява незабавно. При престой извън разрешения срок под 30 дни и продължаващо първоначално основание чл. 31, ал. 3 допуска законовия път за ново кандидатстване след налагане на санкция. Той не удължава задна дата предишното разрешение и не отменя наказанието. При изчисляване на периода за постоянно пребиваване остава и законовото приспадане на една година.

Правните източници са проверени на 24 октомври 2026 г.; преводът е подготвен на 25 октомври 2026 г. Материалът описва общи процедури и категорийни изключения, без да определя отделен случай. За жителите на континентален Китай, Хонконг и Макао и за гражданите на Република Китай без домакинска регистрация важат отделни режими.

sourceHints.text: Can you stay until the expiry date printed on your Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) if the job, course or family relationship supporting it ends sooner? Immigration Act Article 31 requires the National Immigration Agency (NIA) to revoke residence permission and cancel the card when the reason for residence disappears, subject to the statutory grounds on which NIA may approve continued residence.

Some programs allow an earlier renewal application. A qualifying entrepreneur ARC extension for a continuing Taiwan business can be filed during the four months before expiry. The separate continued-residence route after that business ceases has a three-month advance window. Gold Card renewal opens four months before expiry.

An ordinary extension requires the form, passport, existing ARC, photograph and current evidence of the reason for residence. NIA's guide calls for employment, study or family documents as appropriate, plus new address evidence if you have moved.

Continued residence may also be available under Article 31, including specified circumstances involving a deceased family sponsor, domestic violence, children in Taiwan, labor litigation or an occupational injury. Each ground has its own conditions, so a divorce or employment dispute alone does not establish either a right to remain or an inevitable obligation to leave.

An initial email to Hovering International Law Firm at wei@hoveringlaw.com.tw about an employment or family dispute affecting residence should state the event and relevant dates. Leave passport numbers and original identity documents out of that message.

A renewed passport requires a corresponding update to NIA's records, as its passport-renewal FAQ explains. For a data change, NIA's checklist requires the application, photograph, passport and evidence of the change. Keeping the old passport or a copy helps connect the old and new records.

Loss abroad also affects the return journey. Before attempting to travel back, contact NIA and the relevant Taiwan overseas mission with your passport details, an ARC copy if available, and intended return date. They can identify which document your circumstances require.

Re-entry requires valid permission under Immigration Act Article 34. Article 20 of the residence regulations ties that permission to the ARC's validity period and cancels it when the ARC is canceled. The permission recorded with the card therefore needs to cover the intended return date, along with the passport and residence status.

Legal sources checked October 24, 2026. This guide describes foreign-national procedures and category-specific exceptions, without determining an individual case. Mainland China residents, Hong Kong and Macau residents, and ROC nationals without household registration follow separate frameworks.
NIA, new immigrant FAQs, questions 2 and 3: card loss and passport updates.
Taiwan overseas mission directory: offices for overseas inquiries.
Passport updates and replacement cards

The general extension window opens three months before authorized residence expires. Gold Card renewal and qualifying entrepreneur ARC extensions for a continuing Taiwan business have separate four-month windows. These are advance filing periods, not grace periods after expiry.
Can I return to Taiwan with an ARC renewal receipt?

A receipt should not be assumed to replace the required travel documents. Before departure, ask NIA what document covers your return if the renewed card is still pending. Your passport, residence status and re-entry permission must cover the journey.

Primer ARC a Taiwan: sol·licitud i terminis
El termini del primer ARC depèn de com heu entrat i de quan s’ha expedit el visat. El motiu de residència determina els documents i la via de sol·licitud.
Un llibret de viatge sense identificacions, una carpeta de documents i una targeta petita en blanc sobre una taula de tràmits.
Escena fictícia
Des de quin dia es compta el termini del primer ARC?

Si entreu amb visat de resident i obteniu permís de residència, els trenta dies es compten des de l’endemà de l’entrada. Si el visat de resident s’expedeix després d’arribar a Taiwan, BOCA compta trenta dies des de la data d’expedició. Qui sol·licita directament la residència com a visitant ha de complir les condicions i els terminis de la seva categoria.
Quant costa el primer ARC?

La taxa ordinària és de NT$1.000 per cada any de vigència aprovat; una fracció inferior a un any es cobra com un any. Les sol·licituds després d’entrar sense visat o amb visat de visitant tenen un recàrrec de NT$2.200 segons les normes de taxes. Poden correspondre les reduccions o exempcions previstes expressament.
Puc començar a treballar quan rebi l’ARC?

Només si la feina concreta i l’ocupador queden coberts pel permís de treball o per una exempció aplicable. L’ARC acredita la residència, però no concedeix per si mateix una autorització laboral sense límits.

faq.q: When does the deadline for my first ARC start?

If the resident visa is issued after you arrive, BOCA's guidance counts 30 days from its issuance. Visitors applying directly for residence must meet the eligibility and filing rules for their category.

faq.q: How much does a first ARC cost?
faq.a: The standard charge is NT$1,000 for each year of approved validity; a period under one year is charged as one year. Applications after visa-exempt or visitor-visa entry carry an additional NT$2,200 under the fee rules. Specified reductions and exemptions may apply.

faq.q: Can I start work once I receive an ARC?
faq.a: Only if the actual job and employer are covered by the permit or exemption that applies to you. An ARC records residence permission; it does not by itself establish unrestricted work rights.

sourcePassages.text: Thirty days is the filing period for your first Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) if you enter Taiwan on a resident visa and receive residence permission. Count from the day after arrival. Immigration Act Article 22 requires the application to the National Immigration Agency (NIA), which issues the card as evidence of approved residence.

Visitors have a different starting point: they must qualify for a permitted change to residence before they can apply. Holding a valid combined document with ARC functions, such as an Employment Gold Card, removes the need for a separate card under the exception in Article 22.
Your visa and entry record determine the deadline. Someone who receives a resident visa while already in Taiwan uses a different starting date from someone who arrives with one.
Entry and visa status
When to apply
Entered with a resident visa
Within 30 days counted from the day after entry.
Received a resident visa after arriving in Taiwan
Within 30 days from the resident visa's issuance date, under BOCA's guidance.
Entered visa-exempt or with a visitor visa
Before the permitted stay expires, subject to the eligibility and filing rules for the residence category.

NIA's residence guide and BOCA's resident-visa guidance explain the first two situations. For eligible professionals, Article 16 of the Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals permits a direct NIA residence application after visitor-visa or visa-exempt entry, with work authorization or an applicable exemption. Eligibility is specific to that route; the work, study and family comparison explains the conditions for other applicants.

An application based on a resident visa needs the form, photograph, passport and resident visa, evidence of the reason for residence, and proof of your current address, according to NIA's checklist. Bring the required originals and copies. A lease is one accepted address document.
The supporting evidence depends on why you are staying:
Employment: the relevant work approval and a certificate of employment issued within the preceding month, or evidence of the applicable exemption.
Degree study: an admission letter before registration, or recent enrollment evidence once registered.
Family residence: marriage or birth records proving the relationship, together with the sponsoring family member's identity or residence documents.

For a first application through marriage to a Taiwan national with household registration, the Taiwan spouse must attend. NIA also requires proof that the marriage is registered in Taiwan and gives the first spouse-based card one-year validity. These requirements appear in the NIA guide; the Taiwan-spouse residence article covers the family documents in more detail.

Certificates issued abroad may take longer to prepare than the application form. NIA requires authentication of overseas documents and may ask for a Chinese translation verified or notarized in the prescribed manner. The Taiwan overseas mission responsible for the place of issue can explain the authentication procedure. Police certificates and health examinations depend on the particular visa or residence category; they are not required in every first-card application.

NIA's residence application directory separates general residence applications from those for professionals and their dependents, students, and migrant workers. Each category has a designated online system or service-center procedure. Using the professional-worker system is appropriate only if your employment category belongs there.

Students use a dedicated online procedure. For the ordinary in-person application, the relevant NIA service center is the one covering your current address; NIA specifically directs Taiwan-spouse applications there in its residence guide.
Keep the submission record and uploaded documents. If NIA requests further evidence, retaining the request with the original file makes it clear which documents still need to be supplied.

Standard ARC fees are NT$1,000 for each year of approved validity, with a period under one year charged as a full year. Article 3 of the immigration permit fee standards adds NT$2,200 for applications following visa-exempt or visitor-visa entry. Its reduction for overseas compatriot students applies to that status, not to international students generally.

NIA decides the approved term. The ordinary statutory maximum is three years, while qualifying specialist professionals have a separate maximum under their legislation (Immigration Act Article 22; Foreign Professionals Act Article 8). Paying a higher fee cannot establish eligibility for a longer period.

For general applications, NIA gives a processing time of ten working days, excluding document return, requests for additional documents and interviews. The processing period starts again after the additional documents are submitted. Online categories have their own schedules, which may affect travel plans while the application is pending.

Under the student online procedure, payment is due within five working days from approval. A student collecting a smart-chip ARC must print the online payment receipt and take it to the selected NIA service center three working days after payment. That timetable applies to this student procedure; other applicants should follow the method and identification requirements in their approval or collection notice.

Check the issued card against your application. The name, passport details, address and residence expiry date should match the approved particulars; keep the receipt and decision with your immigration records.

An ARC alone does not authorize every job. Before starting work, the relevant permit or exemption must cover the actual employment under Employment Service Act Articles 43 and 48. Once you have the card, its expiry date and any later changes to your address or employment determine the next filings; travel may also require attention to re-entry permission. Those situations are covered in the renewal and changes guide.

Sources checked October 24, 2026. This procedural guide concerns foreign nationals and does not determine individual eligibility. Mainland China residents, Hong Kong and Macau residents, and ROC nationals without household registration follow separate frameworks.

For entry with a resident visa and residence permission, the 30-day period starts the day after arrival. If the resident visa is issued after you arrive, BOCA's guidance counts 30 days from its issuance. Visitors applying directly for residence must meet the eligibility and filing rules for their category.
How much does a first ARC cost?

The standard charge is NT$1,000 for each year of approved validity; a period under one year is charged as one year. Applications after visa-exempt or visitor-visa entry carry an additional NT$2,200 under the fee rules. Specified reductions and exemptions may apply.
Can I start work once I receive an ARC?
Only if the actual job and employer are covered by the permit or exemption that applies to you. An ARC records residence permission; it does not by itself establish unrestricted work rights.

Thirty days is the filing period for your first Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) if you enter Taiwan on a resident visa and receive residence permission. Count from the day after arrival. [Immigration Act Article 22](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawSingle.aspx?pcode=D0080132&flno=22) requires the application to the National Immigration Agency (NIA), which issues the card as evidence of approved residence.

Visitors have a different starting point: they must qualify for a permitted change to residence before they can apply. Holding a valid combined document with ARC functions, such as an Employment Gold Card, removes the need for a separate card under the exception in [Article 22](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawSingle.aspx?pcode=D0080132&flno=22).

## Which date starts the application period?

Your visa and entry record determine the deadline. Someone who receives a resident visa while already in Taiwan uses a different starting date from someone who arrives with one.

| Entry and visa status | When to apply |
|---|---|
| Entered with a resident visa | Within 30 days counted from the day after entry. |
| Received a resident visa after arriving in Taiwan | Within 30 days from the resident visa's issuance date, under BOCA's guidance. |
| Entered visa-exempt or with a visitor visa | Before the permitted stay expires, subject to the eligibility and filing rules for the residence category. |

[NIA's residence guide](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/141970) and [BOCA's resident-visa guidance](https://www.boca.gov.tw/cp-166-276-48430-2.html) explain the first two situations. For eligible professionals, [Article 16 of the Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals](https://law.moj.gov.tw/ENG/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=A0030295) permits a direct NIA residence application after visitor-visa or visa-exempt entry, with work authorization or an applicable exemption. Eligibility is specific to that route; the [work, study and family comparison](/en/columns/taiwan-visa-residence-work-study-family) explains the conditions for other applicants.

## Documents that establish your residence basis

An application based on a resident visa needs the form, photograph, passport and resident visa, evidence of the reason for residence, and proof of your current address, according to [NIA's checklist](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/141970). Bring the required originals and copies. A lease is one accepted address document.

The supporting evidence depends on why you are staying:

- Employment: the relevant work approval and a certificate of employment issued within the preceding month, or evidence of the applicable exemption.
- Degree study: an admission letter before registration, or recent enrollment evidence once registered.
- Family residence: marriage or birth records proving the relationship, together with the sponsoring family member's identity or residence documents.

For a first application through marriage to a Taiwan national with household registration, the Taiwan spouse must attend. NIA also requires proof that the marriage is registered in Taiwan and gives the first spouse-based card one-year validity. These requirements appear in the [NIA guide](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/141970); the [Taiwan-spouse residence article](/en/columns/taiwan-foreign-spouse-residence) covers the family documents in more detail.

Certificates issued abroad may take longer to prepare than the application form. NIA requires authentication of overseas documents and may ask for a Chinese translation verified or notarized in the prescribed manner. The [Taiwan overseas mission responsible for the place of issue](https://www.boca.gov.tw/sp-foof-countrylp-01-2.html) can explain the authentication procedure. Police certificates and health examinations depend on the particular visa or residence category; they are not required in every first-card application.

## Where the application goes

NIA's [residence application directory](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5382/5385/7244/7250/7317/%E5%B1%85%E7%95%99/) separates general residence applications from those for professionals and their dependents, students, and migrant workers. Each category has a designated online system or service-center procedure. Using the professional-worker system is appropriate only if your employment category belongs there.

Students use a [dedicated online procedure](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/417829/cp_news). For the ordinary in-person application, the relevant NIA service center is the one covering your current address; NIA specifically directs Taiwan-spouse applications there in its [residence guide](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/141970).

Keep the submission record and uploaded documents. If NIA requests further evidence, retaining the request with the original file makes it clear which documents still need to be supplied.

## Fees, processing and collection

Standard ARC fees are NT$1,000 for each year of approved validity, with a period under one year charged as a full year. [Article 3 of the immigration permit fee standards](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=D0080135) adds NT$2,200 for applications following visa-exempt or visitor-visa entry. Its reduction for overseas compatriot students applies to that status, not to international students generally.

NIA decides the approved term. The ordinary statutory maximum is three years, while qualifying specialist professionals have a separate maximum under their legislation ([Immigration Act Article 22](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawSingle.aspx?pcode=D0080132&flno=22); [Foreign Professionals Act Article 8](https://law.moj.gov.tw/ENG/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=A0030295)). Paying a higher fee cannot establish eligibility for a longer period.

For general applications, [NIA gives a processing time of ten working days](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/141970), excluding document return, requests for additional documents and interviews. The processing period starts again after the additional documents are submitted. Online categories have their own schedules, which may affect travel plans while the application is pending.

Under the [student online procedure](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/417829/cp_news), payment is due within five working days from approval. A student collecting a smart-chip ARC must print the online payment receipt and take it to the selected NIA service center three working days after payment. That timetable applies to this student procedure; other applicants should follow the method and identification requirements in their approval or collection notice.

Check the issued card against your application. The name, passport details, address and residence expiry date should match the approved particulars; keep the receipt and decision with your immigration records.

An ARC alone does not authorize every job. Before starting work, the relevant permit or exemption must cover the actual employment under [Employment Service Act Articles 43 and 48](https://law.moj.gov.tw/ENG/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=N0090001). Once you have the card, its expiry date and any later changes to your address or employment determine the next filings; travel may also require attention to re-entry permission. Those situations are covered in the [renewal and changes guide](/en/columns/taiwan-arc-renewal-changes-reentry).

Sources checked October 24, 2026. This procedural guide concerns foreign nationals and does not determine individual eligibility. Mainland China residents, Hong Kong and Macau residents, and ROC nationals without household registration follow separate frameworks.

## Official sources

- [Immigration Act, Article 22](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawSingle.aspx?pcode=D0080132&flno=22): first-card deadline, integrated-document exception and ordinary validity limit.
- [NIA, residence, extension and change applications](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/141970), updated April 14, 2026: documents, fees, processing and spouse attendance.
- [BOCA, resident visas for professional employees](https://www.boca.gov.tw/cp-166-276-48430-2.html): ARC timing following resident visa issuance in Taiwan.
- [Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals](https://law.moj.gov.tw/ENG/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=A0030295), Articles 8 and 16: specialist validity and direct residence applications.
- [NIA, residence application directory](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5382/5385/7244/7250/7317/%E5%B1%85%E7%95%99/): category-specific application channels.
- [NIA, student online applications](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/417829/cp_news), updated August 28, 2026: student filing, payment and collection.
- [Taiwan overseas mission directory](https://www.boca.gov.tw/sp-foof-countrylp-01-2.html): document authentication inquiries.
- [Immigration permit fee standards](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=D0080135), Article 3: ARC fees and specified reductions.
- [Employment Service Act](https://law.moj.gov.tw/ENG/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=N0090001), Articles 43 and 48: work authorization and exemptions.

Les sol·licituds presencials ordinàries es presenten al centre de serveis de la NIA competent per l’adreça actual. La [guia general](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/141970) hi remet expressament les sol·licituds de cònjuges de nacionals taiwanesos.

Conserveu el justificant i els documents enviats. Si arriba un requeriment, la còpia de la sol·licitud permet identificar què s’havia aportat i què falta, sense reconstruir l’expedient de memòria.

En aquest procediment general, la [guia xinesa de la NIA](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5385/7244/7250/7317/%E5%B1%85%E7%95%99/29996/) fixa quinze dies naturals per esmenar els defectes, comptats des de l’endemà de la notificació. Quan els documents mancants o incorrectes s’han de sol·licitar a l’estranger, a la Xina continental, Hong Kong o Macau, el termini d’esmena és de tres mesos. Substitueix el termini ordinari. Si l’esmena no arriba dins del termini o continua incompleta, la sol·licitud es denega.

## La taxa segueix la vigència aprovada

La taxa ordinària és de NT$1.000 per any de vigència aprovat. Una durada inferior a un any es cobra com un any sencer. L’[article 3 de les normes de taxes d’immigració](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=D0080135) afegeix NT$2.200 a les sol·licituds després d’una entrada sense visat o amb visat de visitant. Són dòlars taiwanesos. La taxa anual de l’ARC es redueix a la meitat per als estudiants d’ultramar amb l’estatus específic de 僑生; la reducció no correspon a tots els estudiants internacionals.

La NIA decideix la durada. El límit ordinari és de tres anys segons l’[article 22](https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawSingle.aspx?pcode=D0080132&flno=22). Per al professional estranger especialista contractat i els familiars que compleixen els requisits, l’[article 8 de la llei de professionals estrangers](https://law.moj.gov.tw/ENG/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=A0030295) permet una vigència màxima de cinc anys comptats des de l’endemà de l’aprovació de residència per la NIA. Pagar una taxa superior no amplia aquests límits.

## La resolució, el pagament i la targeta

Deu dies hàbils és el termini que [la NIA indica per a la tramitació general](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/141970), sense comptar el temps de retorn de documents, esmenes ni entrevistes. El còmput dels deu dies torna a començar després d’aportar l’esmena, com també precisa la [guia xinesa](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5385/7244/7250/7317/%E5%B1%85%E7%95%99/29996/). Aquesta previsió no garanteix que la targeta estigui disponible per a un vol concret.

Els [expedients electrònics d’estudiants](https://www.immigration.gov.tw/5475/5478/141465/141808/417829/cp_news) tenen un termini indicat de tramitació de cinc dies hàbils, que es reinicia després d’aportar les esmenes. El pagament s’ha de fer dins d’un termini de cinc dies hàbils comptat des de l’aprovació. Si s’emet un ARC electrònic de sis mesos o menys, es descarrega i s’imprimeix després de pagar. Per recollir una targeta amb xip cal imprimir el rebut electrònic i portar-lo al centre de la NIA escollit, tres dies hàbils després del pagament. Els altres sol·licitants han de seguir les instruccions de la seva resolució o avís de recollida.

Abans de començar a treballar, el permís o l’exempció ha de cobrir la feina i l’ocupador concrets d’acord amb els [articles 43 i 48 de la Llei de serveis d’ocupació](https://law.moj.gov.tw/ENG/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=N0090001). L’ARC acredita la residència. Els canvis d’adreça, feina i plans de viatge es tracten a l’[article sobre renovació, canvis i reentrada](/ca/columns/taiwan-arc-renewal-changes-reentry).

Quan rebeu la targeta, contrasteu el nom, les dades del passaport, l’adreça i la caducitat amb el que s’ha aprovat. El rebut i la resolució permeten comprovar després quin període de residència es va concedir.

Fonts oficials contrastades el 24 i el 25 d’octubre de 2026. Aquesta descripció de tràmits per a estrangers no determina l’admissibilitat d’un expedient individual. Les persones de la Xina continental, Hong Kong i Macau, i els nacionals taiwanesos sense registre familiar, segueixen règims específics.

sourceEvidence.text: For entry with a resident visa and residence permission, the 30-day period starts the day after arrival. If the resident visa is issued after you arrive, BOCA's guidance counts 30 days from its issuance. Visitors applying directly for residence must meet the eligibility and filing rules for their category.

The standard charge is NT$1,000 for each year of approved validity; a period under one year is charged as one year. Applications after visa-exempt or visitor-visa entry carry an additional NT$2,200 under the fee rules. Specified reductions and exemptions may apply.

Thirty days is the filing period for your first Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) if you enter Taiwan on a resident visa and receive residence permission. Count from the day after arrival. Immigration Act Article 22 requires the application to the National Immigration Agency (NIA), which issues the card as evidence of approved residence.

Visitors have a different starting point: they must qualify for a permitted change to residence before they can apply. Holding a valid combined document with ARC functions, such as an Employment Gold Card, removes the need for a separate card under the exception in Article 22.
Within 30 days counted from the day after entry.
Within 30 days from the resident visa's issuance date, under BOCA's guidance.

NIA's residence guide and BOCA's resident-visa guidance explain the first two situations. For eligible professionals, Article 16 of the Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals permits a direct NIA residence application after visitor-visa or visa-exempt entry, with work authorization or an applicable exemption. Eligibility is specific to that route; the work, study and family comparison explains the conditions for other applicants.

Standard ARC fees are NT$1,000 for each year of approved validity, with a period under one year charged as a full year. Article 3 of the immigration permit fee standards adds NT$2,200 for applications following visa-exempt or visitor-visa entry. Its reduction for overseas compatriot students applies to that status, not to international students generally.

NIA decides the approved term. The ordinary statutory maximum is three years, while qualifying specialist professionals have a separate maximum under their legislation (Immigration Act Article 22; Foreign Professionals Act Article 8). Paying a higher fee cannot establish eligibility for a longer period.

An ARC alone does not authorize every job. Before starting work, the relevant permit or exemption must cover the actual employment under Employment Service Act Articles 43 and 48. Once you have the card, its expiry date and any later changes to your address or employment determine the next filings; travel may also require attention to re-entry permission. Those situations are covered in the renewal and changes guide.

Your visa and entry record determine the deadline. Someone who receives a resident visa while already in Taiwan uses a different starting date from someone who arrives with one.
Received a resident visa after arriving in Taiwan

An application based on a resident visa needs the form, photograph, passport and resident visa, evidence of the reason for residence, and proof of your current address, according to NIA's checklist. Bring the required originals and copies. A lease is one accepted address document.

For a first application through marriage to a Taiwan national with household registration, the Taiwan spouse must attend. NIA also requires proof that the marriage is registered in Taiwan and gives the first spouse-based card one-year validity. These requirements appear in the NIA guide; the Taiwan-spouse residence article covers the family documents in more detail.

Certificates issued abroad may take longer to prepare than the application form. NIA requires authentication of overseas documents and may ask for a Chinese translation verified or notarized in the prescribed manner. The Taiwan overseas mission responsible for the place of issue can explain the authentication procedure. Police certificates and health examinations depend on the particular visa or residence category; they are not required in every first-card application.

Students use a dedicated online procedure. For the ordinary in-person application, the relevant NIA service center is the one covering your current address; NIA specifically directs Taiwan-spouse applications there in its residence guide.

Check the issued card against your application. The name, passport details, address and residence expiry date should match the approved particulars; keep the receipt and decision with your immigration records.

Visat i residència a Taiwan: treball, estudis i família
La feina prevista, el tipus d’estudis i la situació del familiar a Taiwan determinen la via de residència. La modalitat d’entrada també en condiciona l’accés.
Un ordinador portàtil tancat, llibres i dues tasses al costat d’un llibret de viatge sense identificacions.
Escena fictícia
Puc sol·licitar la residència després d’entrar sense visat?

L’article 16 de la Llei per a la captació i l’ocupació de professionals estrangers permet la sol·licitud directa a la NIA a professionals que compleixen els requisits i tenen permís de treball o una exempció aplicable, i a determinats familiars. La modalitat d’entrada també ha de ser admissible. Les vies ordinàries d’estudis reglats i de mandarí tenen altres requisits de visat.
Quant temps he d’estudiar mandarí abans de demanar l’ARC?

Cal el visat de visitant adequat per a aquests estudis, haver completat quatre mesos en un centre de llengua vinculat a una universitat reconeguda i estar matriculat almenys tres mesos més. També s’han de complir els requisits d’hores, assistència i documents. La matrícula sola no és suficient.
Qualsevol titular d’un ARC pot obtenir residència per al cònjuge?

No. Importen la nacionalitat i la categoria de residència de la persona de Taiwan, el vincle familiar i la situació d’entrada del sol·licitant. La família d’un professional estranger té una regulació diferent de la del cònjuge d’un nacional taiwanès. La llei exclou determinades categories de persones reagrupants.

source.seoTitle: Taiwan Residence for Work, Study and Family
source.summary: Taiwan residence rules for work, study and family depend on the proposed activity, sponsor and entry visa. Eligibility needs to be settled before travel.

faq.q: Can I apply for residence after entering Taiwan visa-exempt?
faq.a: Article 16 of the Foreign Professionals Act allows qualifying professionals with work authorization or an exemption, and certain family members, to apply directly to NIA. Eligibility also depends on the entry arrangement used. Ordinary degree-study and Mandarin-study routes have different entry requirements.

faq.q: How long must I study Mandarin before applying for an ARC?
faq.a: The residence route requires the appropriate study visitor visa, four completed months at a qualifying university-affiliated language center, and registration for at least three further months. Classroom hours, attendance and the required supporting documents also form part of the application conditions. Enrollment alone is insufficient.

faq.q: Can every ARC holder sponsor a spouse for residence?
faq.a: No. The sponsor's nationality and residence category, the relationship and the applicant's entry status all affect eligibility. The rules for a foreign professional's family differ from those for a spouse of a Taiwan national, and statutory exclusions apply to some sponsors.

sourcePassages.text: Visa-exempt entry may suit a qualifying professional who intends to apply for residence in Taiwan, but it can rule out the ordinary in-country application for a degree or Mandarin student. Foreign Professionals Act Article 16 permits the professional route; BOCA's degree-study and Mandarin-study guidance set different entry conditions for students.
Nationality and the passport used determine visa eligibility. The Taiwan overseas mission handling your application provides the nationality-specific requirements and document procedures.

A temporary visitor's permitted activities and length of stay depend on the entry arrangement granted. A longer move requires a residence basis, such as employment, study or joining family. BOCA's resident-visa guidance covers those purposes, while the National Immigration Agency (NIA) decides residence applications and issues the Alien Resident Certificate (ARC).
Some eligible visitors can apply directly to NIA. Other applicants need the appropriate visa before entry, so arriving as a visitor leaves no general right to convert a short stay into residence.

For most foreign professional hires, the employer applies for a work permit, subject to statutory exceptions and the authority responsible for the job. Articles 4 and 5 of the Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals define professional work and the permit framework. A signed offer is not work authorization.

Once a qualifying foreign professional or foreign specialist professional has the permit or an applicable exemption, Article 16 allows a direct residence application following visa-exempt or visitor-visa entry. NIA must still approve the residence application before issuing an ARC. The current Article 16 took effect on January 1, 2026, as recorded in the Act's legislative history.

NIA's guide excludes trial visa exemptions, the Southeast Asian online travel-authorization scheme and other listed entry arrangements from this direct-application route unless another rule applies, even where the applicant holds work approval.

Care work, fishing and other migrant-worker categories under Employment Service Act Article 46 have their own rules. NIA's migrant-worker residence procedure applies to those categories; employment in Taiwan does not by itself place a worker within the foreign-professional scheme. The category on the work approval identifies which procedure to use.

Full-time foreign students applying from abroad can seek a resident visa at a Taiwan overseas mission. Those who enter on a visitor visa specifically for foreign-student study may apply directly to NIA for residence. The ordinary in-country study route in BOCA's student guidance excludes visa-exempt entry, landing visas and visitor visas issued for other purposes.

Depending on the application, BOCA also requires educational records, financial evidence and a health certificate alongside the admission letter; the program's checklist determines which overseas records need authentication.

For Mandarin learners, the language-study visitor visa ordinarily comes before arrival. Eligibility for residence follows four completed months at a qualifying university-affiliated center, with registration for at least three more months. BOCA's Mandarin residence guidance requires at least 15 classroom hours a week, Monday through Friday. Absences, including leave, may not exceed one quarter of class hours. Tuition payment alone does not establish eligibility.

Can a student take a part-time job? Employment Service Act Articles 43 and 50 govern work permits and specified student employment. The admission letter and student ARC do not replace the work authorization needed for the job.

Family residence depends on the sponsor's status and the relationship. For a spouse of a Taiwan national residing in Taiwan with household registration, one in-country route under Immigration Act Article 23 requires a valid visa allowing a stay of at least 60 days and without the specified restrictions. Marriage therefore does not establish a general right to convert visa-exempt entry to residence. The required relationship documents and related status issues appear in residence through a Taiwan spouse.

When a foreign professional engaged in professional work in Taiwan or a foreign specialist professional already has approved residence or permanent residence, Article 16 allows certain family members to apply directly after visa-exempt or visitor-visa entry. It covers a spouse, minor children, and adult children unable to care for themselves because of physical or mental disability. Parents and other adult children are excluded.

Work rights vary by family category. Employment Service Act Article 48 provides a work-permit exemption for an approved resident married to a Taiwan national with household registration. Dependent spouses of foreign professionals cannot assume that exemption applies to them. For qualifying spouses of specialist or senior professionals, Foreign Professionals Act Article 15 provides a direct application for a work permit.

Specialist professionals who meet the program's criteria may qualify for an Employment Gold Card, which combines work, residence, visa and re-entry functions in one document. The Gold Card article covers that application separately.
BOCA publishes the entrepreneur route requirements for applicants planning to establish a business in Taiwan.

Working-holiday access depends on the nationality-specific program. The digital-nomad visitor visa has separate nationality and qualification requirements and does not automatically lead to an ARC. Foreign Professionals Act Article 14 limits that remote-work route to qualifying work without providing services to Taiwan businesses or employers.

Once the residence category and entry requirements are established, the first ARC application guide covers filing and collection. An existing resident moving to a new job, course or family basis also needs the rules on renewal and changes: the current card does not settle whether that new purpose qualifies.

Article 16 of the Foreign Professionals Act allows qualifying professionals with work authorization or an exemption, and certain family members, to apply directly to NIA. Eligibility also depends on the entry arrangement used. Ordinary degree-study and Mandarin-study routes have different entry requirements.
How long must I study Mandarin before applying for an ARC?

The residence route requires the appropriate study visitor visa, four completed months at a qualifying university-affiliated language center, and registration for at least three further months. Classroom hours, attendance and the required supporting documents also form part of the application conditions. Enrollment alone is insufficient.
Can every ARC holder sponsor a spouse for residence?

No. The sponsor's nationality and residence category, the relationship and the applicant's entry status all affect eligibility. The rules for a foreign professional's family differ from those for a spouse of a Taiwan national, and statutory exclusions apply to some sponsors.

targetPassages.text: Quatre mesos d’estudi de mandarí en un centre de llengua vinculat a una universitat reconeguda són un dels requisits per passar a la residència per aquesta via. També cal haver entrat amb el visat de visitant adequat per estudiar mandarí i continuar matriculat almenys tres mesos més, segons la guia de BOCA. Pagar el curs no resol totes aquestes condicions.

Per a un professional estranger que compleix l’article 16 de la Llei per a la captació i l’ocupació de professionals estrangers, una entrada sense visat pot donar pas a una sol·licitud directa de residència amb permís de treball o una exempció aplicable. Els estudiants segueixen altres regles d’entrada. El passaport i l’activitat prevista s’han de considerar conjuntament abans de viatjar.

La nacionalitat i el passaport utilitzat determinen els requisits de visat. Consulteu la representació taiwanesa que rep la sol·licitud per confirmar les condicions aplicables i els tràmits dels documents estrangers.

Durant una visita, la durada i les activitats admeses depenen de l’autorització d’entrada. Per establir-se a Taiwan cal un motiu de residència, com ara feina, estudis o reagrupament familiar. BOCA tramita els visats de resident; l’Agència Nacional d’Immigració, la NIA, resol la residència i expedeix el certificat ARC.

Algunes categories poden presentar-se directament a la NIA. Altres necessiten el visat adequat abans d’entrar. No hi ha un dret general de qualsevol visitant a convertir una estada curta en residència.

Normalment, l’ocupador demana el permís de treball quan contracta un professional estranger. S’hi apliquen les excepcions legals i la distribució de competències pròpia de cada feina. Els articles 4 i 5 de la llei de professionals estrangers defineixen les activitats professionals i el règim de permisos. L’oferta no substitueix l’autorització.

El professional estranger o professional estranger especialista que disposa del permís o d’una exempció aplicable per al treball professional pot utilitzar l’article 16 després d’una entrada admissible sense visat o amb visat de visitant. La NIA ha d’aprovar la residència abans d’expedir l’ARC. L’historial d’entrada en vigor situa l’inici de vigència de la versió actual d’aquest article a l’1 de gener de 2026.

La guia de la NIA exclou d’aquesta via directa les exempcions de visat experimentals, el sistema d’autorització electrònica de viatge per al sud-est asiàtic i les altres modalitats indicades, tret que una altra disposició aplicable ho permeti. Tenir permís de treball no elimina aquesta condició d’entrada.

Les feines de cures, pesca i altres categories de treballadors migrants regulades per l’article 46 de la Llei de serveis d’ocupació segueixen règims propis. La NIA té un procediment de residència per a aquests treballadors. Consulteu la categoria indicada en l’autorització laboral per situar el tràmit: treballar a Taiwan no converteix automàticament una persona en professional estranger als efectes d’aquesta llei.

En la via electrònica específica de professionals i familiars, sortir de Taiwan durant l’examen posa fi a la tramitació. Després del retorn es pot presentar una nova sol·licitud si es compleixen els requisits d’aquell procediment. Aquesta regla no garanteix la reentrada ni imposa una prohibició general de viatjar a tots els sol·licitants d’ARC.

Per al cònjuge d’un nacional taiwanès que resideix a Taiwan i hi té registre familiar, l’article 23 de la Llei d’immigració preveu una via de sol·licitud dins del país. Requereix un visat vàlid que autoritzi una estada d’almenys seixanta dies, sense prohibició de pròrroga ni les altres restriccions previstes. El matrimoni, per si sol, no permet convertir qualsevol entrada sense visat en residència. També cal considerar les exclusions legals vinculades a la situació de la persona reagrupant. La guia sobre residència amb un cònjuge taiwanès, en anglès, desenvolupa els documents.
L’article 16 de la llei de professionals estrangers defineix una altra via familiar. La persona de Taiwan ha de pertànyer a una d’aquestes categories:
Professional estranger que exerceix treball professional a Taiwan.
Professional estranger especialista, dins de la categoria legal «foreign specialist professional».

Totes dues categories requereixen que la NIA hagi aprovat la residència o la residència permanent. El requisit de treball professional actual a Taiwan s’aplica a la primera categoria; aquesta disposició familiar no l’imposa de la mateixa manera a tot especialista.

Poden acollir-s’hi el cònjuge, els fills menors i els fills adults que, per una discapacitat física o mental, no poden tenir cura de si mateixos. També han de complir les condicions de l’entrada sense visat o amb visat de visitant admesa per a aquesta sol·licitud directa. Els progenitors no s’hi inclouen. Tampoc els altres fills adults.

El permís per treballar s’examina segons la categoria familiar. L’article 48 de la Llei de serveis d’ocupació eximeix de permís de treball l’estranger amb residència aprovada que està casat amb un nacional taiwanès amb registre familiar. Aquesta exempció no es pot traslladar automàticament als cònjuges de professionals estrangers. Per al cònjuge d’un professional especialista o d’alt nivell, l’article 15 permet demanar el permís directament al Ministeri de Treball si la NIA ha aprovat la residència familiar. El permís no pot superar la durada d’aquesta residència.

L’estudiant estranger d’estudis reglats a temps complet pot demanar el visat de resident en una representació taiwanesa abans de viatjar. Qui entra amb un visat de visitant específic per a estudis com a estudiant estranger pot sol·licitar la residència directament a la NIA. La via ordinària descrita a la guia de BOCA exclou l’entrada sense visat, el visat expedit a l’arribada i el visat de visitant concedit per a altres finalitats.

Amb el document d’admissió es poden requerir expedients acadèmics, proves de recursos i un certificat de salut. La llista de la categoria concreta també determina quins documents estrangers requereixen autenticació. Aquestes gestions poden començar abans de reservar el viatge.

En els cursos de mandarí, el visat de visitant per estudiar la llengua s’obté normalment abans d’arribar. A més dels quatre mesos completats i la matrícula d’almenys tres mesos més, BOCA exigeix almenys quinze hores setmanals de classe de dilluns a divendres. Les absències, inclosos els permisos d’absència, no poden superar una quarta part de les hores lectives.

Es pot treballar mentre s’estudia? Els articles 43 i 50 de la Llei de serveis d’ocupació regulen l’autorització i les modalitats previstes de feina d’estudiants. La matrícula i l’ARC d’estudiant no substitueixen el permís laboral que calgui per a la feina.

Els especialistes que compleixen els criteris poden sol·licitar una Employment Gold Card. Integra treball, visat, residència i reentrada. L’article 9 de la llei de professionals estrangers en preveu una vigència d’un a tres anys. La guia específica sobre la Gold Card, en anglès, desenvolupa el tràmit.
BOCA publica els requisits de la via per a emprenedors que volen establir una activitat a Taiwan. La disponibilitat del programa de vacances i treball depèn de l’acord corresponent a la nacionalitat.

Obtenir el visat de visitant per a nòmades digitals exigeix complir-ne els requisits de nacionalitat i qualificació; no dona automàticament dret a un ARC. L’article 14 de la llei de professionals estrangers exigeix treball a distància admissible, sense prestar serveis a empreses o ocupadors de Taiwan.

Amb la via i l’entrada identificades, la guia del primer ARC concreta la presentació i la recollida. Si ja teniu residència, passar a una feina, uns estudis o un motiu familiar nou pot exigir els tràmits de canvi de motiu.

Qui prepara els documents familiars ha d’identificar la persona de Taiwan i l’aprovació de residència en què es basarà la petició. En un expedient d’estudis, el visat ha de correspondre al programa al qual us heu matriculat.

Fonts contrastades el 24 i el 25 d’octubre de 2026. L’admissibilitat es resol segons la situació individual. Aquestes vies corresponen a estrangers; la Xina continental, Hong Kong, Macau i els nacionals taiwanesos sense registre familiar tenen règims diferenciats.
Llei per a la captació i l’ocupació de professionals estrangers, articles 4, 5, 9 i 14–16, i historial d’entrada en vigor.
Llei d’immigració, article 23: vies de residència dins de Taiwan.
Llei de serveis d’ocupació, articles 43, 46, 48 i 50.
BOCA: visats de resident, estudiants estrangers, visat de visitant per a mandarí i residència per a aquests estudis.
NIA: residència després d’entrar sense visat o amb visat de visitant, nota 7(1), actualitzada el 14 d’abril de 2026: exclusions de determinades modalitats d’entrada.
NIA: residència de treballadors migrants.
Portal oficial de la Gold Card i requisits de BOCA per a emprenedors.
BOCA: vacances i treball i visat de nòmada digital.
Representacions taiwaneses a l’estranger.
NIA: procediment electrònic de professionals i familiars, advertiment 9: sortida durant l’examen i nova sol·licitud condicionada.
El visat ha de correspondre a l’activitat
La feina i la persona que sol·licita el permís
La persona de Taiwan determina la via familiar
La matrícula i les hores efectives de classe
Gold Card, emprenedoria i estades més llargues
Fonts oficials
Puc sol·licitar la residència després d’entrar sense visat?

L’article 16 de la Llei per a la captació i l’ocupació de professionals estrangers permet la sol·licitud directa a la NIA a professionals que compleixen els requisits i tenen permís de treball o una exempció aplicable, i a determinats familiars. La modalitat d’entrada també ha de ser admissible. Les vies ordinàries d’estudis reglats i de mandarí tenen altres requisits de visat.
Quant temps he d’estudiar mandarí abans de demanar l’ARC?

Cal el visat de visitant adequat per a aquests estudis, haver completat quatre mesos en un centre de llengua vinculat a una universitat reconeguda i estar matriculat almenys tres mesos més. També s’han de complir els requisits d’hores, assistència i documents. La matrícula sola no és suficient.
Qualsevol titular d’un ARC pot obtenir residència per al cònjuge?

No. Importen la nacionalitat i la categoria de residència de la persona de Taiwan, el vincle familiar i la situació d’entrada del sol·licitant. La família d’un professional estranger té una regulació diferent de la del cònjuge d’un nacional taiwanès. La llei exclou determinades categories de persones reagrupants.
